entries.abstract: We present 136 hr of 340 MHz observations of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (HUDF) conducted with the VLA Low-band Ionosphere and Transient Experiment (VLITE), collected commensally with higher-frequency Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observations. Our deepest image combines 20 hr of data, covers 4 square degrees, and achieves an angular resolution of 8.8 arcsec x 3.8 arcsec with an rms sensitivity of 158 microJy per beam at the field center. We catalog 671 radio sources detected above 5 sigma significance. Correcting for incompleteness using injection-recovery simulations with a model radio continuum population, we show that our source counts recover the sub-mJy star-forming galaxy population at abundances consistent with other deep fields at comparable frequencies. The data span 45 observing days across two VLA A-configuration semesters separated by 1.3 years, providing a search for variability on ~1-year timescales at sub-mJy flux densities. We identify eleven variable sources with flux densities of 1-100 mJy and modulation indices of 6-40%, six of which exhibit peaked radio spectra consistent with compact AGN. Their variability amplitudes are consistent with refractive interstellar scintillation (RISS) predicted for this line of sight, though three sources with modulation indices exceeding 30% likely require an intrinsic contribution. One source, subsequently confirmed as a compact symmetric object through VLBA follow-up observations, demonstrates the potential of VLITE for identifying populations of young radio AGN through commensal low-frequency variability searches.

entries.title: Episodic Protostellar Outflows: A Proper Motion Study in Serpens South
entries.abstract: Serpens South is a notable protostellar cluster with signatures of recent star formation, including a high protostellar fraction. Within the region, several protostars provide important mechanical feedback via outflows. We investigate the molecular outflow driven by the Class 0 protostar known as CARMA-7, which is located in the central hub of Serpens South. Two epochs of observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) with sub-arcsecond resolution capture the well-collimated, episodic outflow with distinct ejecta knots. This outflow, traced with 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7, appears to be mostly blueshifted to the south and redshifted to the north, with radial velocities up to at least 25 km/s. We present the first proper motion study of this outflow by comparing observations taken in 2017 and 2021. The measured proper motions trace the ejection history and refine the inferred outflow morphology. We find that proper motions of the 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7 knots range between 10 - 40 mas/yr, corresponding to 30-90 km/s. Using radial velocities and proper motions, we determined that the inclinations of the outflow lobes are ~60 -80 degrees relative to the line of sight. Finally, we measure ejection timescales as recent as ~10 to ~120 years, and we discuss this in the context of other known protostars with recent ejecta events.

entries.title: Chemical and dynamical evolution of prestellar cores, the dawn of star and planet formation
entries.abstract: Studying prestellar cores is crucial to understanding the formation of stellar and planetary systems. To date, we lack a comprehensive survey of their density and velocity structure at small scales (100-1000 au), the gas ionisation state, their lifetimes, and how these properties are influenced by the environment. A deep study into this critical stage of star formation requires a large single-dish (sub)millimetre telescope like AtLAST.

entries.title: The Giant Planet Mass Function Across Stellar Mass and Metallicity: Massive Stars Make Massive Planets
entries.abstract: Although giant planet occurrence correlates with stellar mass and metallicity, it remains unclear whether these properties also shape the companion mass distribution. We investigate this question using 719 FGKM stars from the California Legacy Survey and companion true-mass constraints from radial velocities and Hipparcos-Gaia astrometry. Our hierarchical occurrence analysis accounts for survey completeness and companion parameter uncertainties over giant planet and brown dwarf masses of M_c=0.4-50 M_Jup and semi-major axes of a=0.1-10 AU. We find that, compared to the rate among our full sample of 0.19 +/- 0.02 planets per star in this interval, giant planet occurrence is significantly enhanced around stars with high mass (M_star>1 M_sun; 0.39 (+0.06/-0.05) planets per star) and high metallicity ([Fe/H]>0.0; 0.30 (+0.04/-0.03) planets per star). We find evidence at the 2-3 sigma level that the planet mass function shape varies with stellar mass, with higher characteristic planet masses around stars with M_star>1 M_sun than around lower-mass hosts, based on differences in both the CDFs of fitted models and constraints on model shape parameters. For the full sample, occurrence declines above a few Jupiter masses and is consistent with either a plateau below ~3 M_Jup or a peak near 1-2 M_Jup. The brown dwarf desert begins at a companion-to-host mass ratio of 0.013-0.02. These results suggest that stellar properties influence not only the frequency of giant companions but also their characteristic masses. Within the core accretion framework, this shift could reflect larger gas reservoirs around more massive stars or earlier core formation in metal-rich disks, allowing greater gas accretion before disk dispersal.

entries.title: Episodic Star Formation - II. The Origin of the Fundamental Metallicity Relation
entries.abstract: The Fundamental Metallicity Relation (FMR) extends the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) by including star formation rate (SFR) as a third parameter. At fixed stellar mass, galaxies with higher SFRs tend to have lower gas-phase metallicities. We investigate the physical origin of the FMR in the context of episodic star formation (Gui et al. 2026, paper I of this series) by tracing the evolution histories of 8,979 central star-forming galaxies selected at $z=0$ in TNG100 back to $z=1$. We find that the overall MZR scatter at $z=0$ ($\sim0.11$ dex) comprises both long-lived differences among galaxies ($\sim0.09$ dex) and temporal fluctuations within individual galaxies ($\sim 0.07$ dex). The galaxy-to-galaxy component shows an anticorrelation between SFR and gas-phase metallicity, as shown by the observed FMR. As for the consequence from temporal fluctuation, we track individual histories and stack the upward and downward SFR phases of a refined sample. Time-shift analysis and stacked histories show a well-behaved sequence in which the cold non-star-forming gas reservoir increases (decreases) first, followed by a decrease (increase) in gas-phase metallicity and then a rise (decline) in SFR. This ordering is consistent with a physical scenario where metal-poor gas first replenishes the cold reservoir and dilutes the gas before SFR rises to the peak, followed by feedback-driven gas heating/removal, resulting in a shift in metallicity from dilution to enrichment as SFR decreases towards the valley. This naturally explains the anticorrelation between the SFR and gas-phase metallicities as indicated by the observed FMR.

analysis.reason: This study accurately computes non-thermal electron impact ionization cross sections for Sr and investigates excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell Auger cascades, which directly impacts non-LTE ionization modeling of kilonova ejecta.
analysis.result: Excitation-autoionization (EAI) constitutes roughly half of the total single ionization cross sections for $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $\mathrm{Sr\,II}$, and omitting EAI leads to an error factor of up to $\sim 2$ in the derived ion abundances. Inner-shell ionization accounts for $30\% - 40\%$ of the total cross section in $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $20\% - 30\%$ in $\mathrm{Sr\,II-III}$ at $5\,\mathrm{keV}$, scaling as $\propto \ln(E)/E$ at high energies; incorporating inner-shell ionization and Auger cascades modifies ion fractions by $20\% - 50\%$. Furthermore, approximately $20\% - 30\%$ of heavy atoms (e.g., Te) are ionized beyond triply ionized states at kilonova ejecta temperatures.
analysis.problem: Standard kilonova spectral synthesis often relies on empirical Lotz cross sections ($\sigma_{\mathrm{Lotz}}(E) = \sum_i n_i a_i \frac{\ln(E/I_i)}{E I_i}$) that neglect excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell multi-electron ejection via Auger cascades, introducing significant systematic errors into non-thermal ionization balance and line identification.
analysis.method: Level-resolved (J-split) and configuration-average (CA) electron impact cross sections were computed using the Flexible Atomic Code (FAC) with distorted wave and binary encounter dipole approximations up to $5\,\mathrm{keV}$. These cross sections were integrated into the `pynonthermal` Spencer-Fano solver under an energy deposition rate $q(t) = 0.15 \,(t / 1.4\,\mathrm{days})^{-1.3}\,\mathrm{eV\,s^{-1}\,ion^{-1}}$ to iteratively solve for the degraded electron spectrum $y(E)$ and the non-thermal steady-state ionization balance $\sum_{i \le j} \sum_{k > j-i} n_i \Gamma_{i,k} = n_{j+1} n_e \alpha_{j+1}(T)$.
assumptions: Steady-state balance between non-thermal collisional ionization and radiative/dielectronic recombination in the ejecta
limits: Photoionization, thermal collisional ionization, and charge exchange reactions are omitted from the Spencer-Fano model
citation_leads: 3.1. Single Ionization: Sr I: “The Lotz ionization cross section agrees well near the ionization threshold but fails to account for the enhanced cross section due to excitationautoionization.”

4.1. Spencer-Fano Implementation: “The above ionization balance includes only non-thermal ionization and the supplied recombination rates. Photoionization, thermal collisional ionization, and charge exchange are omitted.”

4.5. Extrapolation to Higher Ion Stages: “full model extrapolated to higher charge states shows that approximately 20 - 30% of the Te atoms are found in charge states above triply ionized at the temperatures expected in KNe ejecta.”
6. Conclusions: “conversion of near-neutral inner shell ionization cross sections into finalion-resolved cross sections leads to changes in near-neutral ion fractions of order 20-50%.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that threshold binning can compress $>10^5$ cross-section channels down to $\sim 35$ with negligible precision loss ($<5\%$), provided complete EAI and inner-shell cross sections for $\mathrm{Sr\,I-III}$, and established the necessity of extending kilonova ionization models to higher charge states (e.g., Te XI).

analysis.reason: This paper presents the Fourier power spectrum injection framework and empirical sensitivity calibration for the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS), characterizing pulse smearing, FDMT chromatic artifacts, and red noise limits relevant to blind pulsar and periodic transient searches.
analysis.result: For stacking depths of 1–30 days, CHAMPSS achieves maximum sensitivity for pulsar spin frequencies $f \approx 0.1\text{--}100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ and flux densities $S \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$. Monthly incoherent stacking increases the transmission fraction of faint sources ($0.1 < S < 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$) by up to $50\%$ (from $0.08\%$ in daily searches to $6.6\%$ in month-long searches). Both coherent and incoherent stacking scale in detection significance as $S_{\mathrm{min}} \propto N_{\mathrm{days}}^{-1/2}$, but red noise degrades the sensitivity at long periods ($P \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{s}$, $f \lesssim 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$) by an order of magnitude compared to standard radiometer equation predictions.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the search completeness and selection effects of all-sky pulsar stacking searches without computationally prohibitive and irreversible raw time-domain signal injections, while accounting for non-astrophysical red noise, scalloping loss, and Fast Dispersion Measure Transform (FDMT) covariance artifacts.
analysis.method: Synthetic signal injection directly into Fourier power spectra across parameter grids of spin frequency $f \in [10^{-3}, 10^{2.7}]\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $\mathrm{DM}$, and flux density $S \in [0.001, 10]\,\mathrm{mJy}$. The pipeline incorporates normalized profile scaling $A = \frac{GS}{(T_{\mathrm{sys}}+T_{\mathrm{sky}})\beta}\sqrt{\frac{n_{\mathrm{days}}}{N_k}}\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{pol}}\Delta\nu\tau}$, effective temporal smearing $\Delta t_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx \sqrt{1.25\Delta t_{\mathrm{samp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{dedisp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{chan}}^2}$, sinc-squared scalloping attenuation $P_j = |a_j|^2 \mathrm{sinc}^2[\pi(r-j)]$, running median red noise normalization, and DBSCAN candidate clustering.

analysis.reason: The paper reports a statistically significant triplet association between a temporally clustered gravitational wave pair (S190910d and S190910h, separated by $7.1\,\mathrm{hr}$) and the Type IIb stripped-envelope supernova SN 2019rsq ($D_{\rm L} = 140.6\,\mathrm{Mpc}$). It introduces a physical collapsar accretion disk fragmentation framework that explains compact binary formation and sequential mergers inside a collapsing massive star's core engine.
analysis.result: The GW pair S190910d and S190910h separated by $\Delta t \simeq 7.1\,\mathrm{hr}$ has a pairwise null chance coincidence probability of $P_{\rm 2GW} = 7.6 \times 10^{-5}$ under 3D localization overlap tests. Parameter inference indicates S190910d is an asymmetric binary with $q \simeq 0.086$, $m_1^{\rm src} \simeq 34\,M_\odot$, and $m_2^{\rm src} \simeq 2.9\,M_\odot$ ($\,\rho_{\rm net} \simeq 8.6$), while S190910h conditioned on the SN position has $m_1^{\rm src} \simeq 2.5\,M_\odot$ and $m_2^{\rm src} \simeq 1.3\,M_\odot$. SN 2019rsq light curve modeling yields an ejecta mass $M_{\rm ej} \simeq 3\,M_\odot$, kinetic energy $E_{\rm K} \simeq 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, and nickel mass $M_{^{56}\mathrm{Ni}} \approx 0.08\text{--}0.1\,M_\odot$.
analysis.reading_entry: 6 Disk fragmentation as a plausible framework
analysis.problem: Whether temporally clustered gravitational wave triggers within hours of each other can physically originate from a single astrophysical progenitor system, specifically connecting stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae with compact binary mergers.
analysis.method:
Bayesian parameter inference with precessing waveform models (IMRPhenomXPHM) and independent pipeline verification (SPIIR, IAS); Monte Carlo 3D directional and line-of-sight distance coincidence significance tests across the ZTF BTS and GW superevent catalogs; radiative hydrodynamics and diffusion modeling (TransFit and SNEC) of SN 2019rsq; analytic modeling of disk gravitational fragmentation and gravitational-wave orbital inspiral timescales:
$$\tau_{\mathrm{NSBH}} = \frac{5}{256} \frac{c^{5} a_{0}^{4}}{G^{3} M_{\bullet}^{2} M_{\mathrm{NS}}} \simeq 1.1\,\mathrm{hr} \left( \frac{R_{\mathrm{form}}}{100 R_{\mathrm{g}}} \right)^{4} \left( \frac{M_{\bullet}}{35 M_{\odot}} \right)^{2} \left( \frac{M_{\mathrm{NS}}}{3 M_{\odot}} \right)^{-1}$$\nand binary fragment coalescence $\tau_{\mathrm{NSNS}} = \frac{5}{512} \frac{c^5 a_0^4}{G^3 M_{\mathrm{NS}}^3}$.
assumptions: A massive rotating stellar core collapses to produce a central black hole surrounded by a gravitationally unstable, neutrino-cooled accretion disk that fragments at radii $R_{\mathrm{form}} \sim 100\text{--}300\,R_g$.
limits: S190910h was significantly detected only in a single detector (LIGO Livingston) during a period of reduced sensitivity in Virgo and Hanford; radio non-detections rule out powerful on-axis GRB 030329-like jets but leave choked, weak, or misaligned outflows unconstrained.
citation_leads: 2 Statistical Significance and Chance Coincidence Tests: “For the 43-superevent selected sample, the empirical probability of an unrelated GW pair occurring within the observed 7.1 hr separation and satisfying the adopted 3D criteria is $P _ { \mathrm { 2 G W } } = 7 . 6 \times 1 0 ^ { - 5 }$ .”

6 Disk fragmentation as a plausible framework: “In the disk fragmentation scenario, a massive rotating star collapses to form a central compact object (typically a black hole) surrounded by a massive gaseous accretion disk, likely within minutes after the core collapse.”
6 Disk fragmentation as a plausible framework: “The resulting direct inspiral time is naturally of order hours to days, depending sensitively on the circularization radius and compact-object masses.”
Supplementary Information: “Temporal proximity plus two-dimensional overlap alone therefore does not necessarily imply a similarly compact three-dimensional configuration.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates quantitatively that rapid multi-fragmentation in collapsar disks naturally produces direct GW inspiral delays of order hours: $\tau_{\rm NSBH} \propto a_0^4 M_\bullet^2 M_{\rm NS}^{-1}$ for fragment-black hole coalescence and $\tau_{\rm NSNS} \propto a_0^4 M_{\rm NS}^{-3}$ for fragment-fragment mergers, establishing a theoretical and observational foundation for clustered GW events in core-collapse supernovae.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Schematic illustration of the proposed fragmenting-disk scenario. a, Core collapse of a rapidly rotating massive star forms a black hole of several tens of solar masses surrounded by a gravitationally unstable accretion disk that fragments at radii of order $100$ – $300R_{g}$. b, An accretion-grown compact fragment or earlier fragment-merger remnant reaches a mass of a few solar masses and inspirals into the central black hole, producing S190910d, while the outer stellar layers expand as SN 2019rsq. Other lower-mass fragments remain in the outer disk and may pair into binaries. c, A low-mass compact binary formed in the disk merges $\simeq 7.1$ hr later, producing S190910h, while the supernova ejecta continue to expand toward the optical peak approximately 24 days after S190910d. d, Subsequent fragment interactions and few-body scattering may produce additional compact-object mergers or delayed central-engine activity on timescales extending from days to weeks or months.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: A rapidly rotating massive star collapses to form a black hole and a gravitationally unstable disk that fragments at radii of order $100$–$300R_g$. A fragment or fragment-merger remnant can grow to a few solar masses and inspiral into the central black hole, while other fragments may form a low-mass binary that merges about $7.1$ hr later. The scenario connects these mergers with the expanding ejecta of SN 2019rsq and allows for further delayed interactions.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Three dimensional localization overlap of S190910d, S190910h, and SN 2019rsq. Left panel: Sky localizations of S190910d (grey) and S190910h (orange) shown as 90% credible regions. The overlapping region contains the position of SN 2019rsq, marked by the red box. right upper Panel: Host galaxy environment of SN 2019rsq. The location of the supernova is indicated by the red plus. The image was obtained from the DESI archival service. Lower right panel: Line-of-sight distance information evaluated at the SN coordinates from the public 3D GW localization products. For visualization, the grey and orange curves show the Gaussian likelihood kernels associated with the per-pixel radial-ansatz parameters $(\mu,\sigma)$ for S190910d $(372.37,174.57)$ Mpc and S190910h $(172.60,78.55)$ Mpc. After removal of the common volumetric $D_{L}^{2}$ prior, their product gives an approximate common-distance likelihood centred at $D_{\rm comb}=206.23\pm 71.63$ Mpc (green; Methods, Section 2 ). The red vertical line marks the redshift distance of SN 2019rsq, $D_{\rm SN}=140.6$ Mpc, which lies within the broad support of this consistency estimate. This construction is not a formal joint parameter-estimation posterior.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: The 90% sky localizations of S190910d and S190910h overlap at the position of SN 2019rsq. At the supernova coordinates, the approximate common-distance likelihood is centered at $D_{\rm comb}=206.23\pm71.63$ Mpc, and the supernova redshift distance, $D_{\rm SN}=140.6$ Mpc, lies within its broad support. The caption cautions that this is not a formal joint parameter-estimation posterior.

analysis.reason: This study develops a unified dual-branch mass-loading framework reconciling coherent electron-cyclotron maser emission (ECME) and magnetic accretion X-ray modulation in the long-period radio transient and cataclysmic variable ASKAP J1745-5051.
analysis.result: The high mass-loading branch reproduces the phased X-ray modulation with pulsed fractions of $28.00\%$ (0.3–1.5 keV) and $16.15\%$ (1.5–10 keV) through accretion curtain absorption and soft-cap beaming ($k_{\rm B}T_{\rm cap} \approx 0.14~{\rm keV}$, $k_{\rm B}T_{\rm sh} \approx 15~{\rm keV}$). The low mass-loading branch fed by donor stellar wind ($\dot{M}_{\rm w} = 10^{-14}~M_\odot~{\rm yr}^{-1}$) maintains a low density $n_{\rm e} \sim (1-4) \times 10^7~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, satisfying $\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_B \sim 0.03-0.06 \le 0.3$ and producing coherent ECME pulses at $\nu_{\rm obs} = 1~{\rm GHz}$ ($B \approx 373-392~{\rm G}$).
analysis.problem: How coherent radio pulses characteristic of long-period transients (LPTs) can coexist with dense Roche-lobe overflow accretion and modulated X-ray emission at an identical $P_{\rm orb} \approx 82~{\rm min}$ period in ASKAP J1745-5051 without quenching the electron-cyclotron maser.
analysis.method: Constructed a 3D binary magnetospheric model combining the magnetic fields $\boldsymbol{B}_{\rm tot} = \boldsymbol{B}_1 + \boldsymbol{B}_2$ of the white dwarf and donor star. Derived the mass-loading rate per unit flux $\Lambda = \rho_{\rm load} v_{\rm load} / B_{\rm load}$ where magnetic pressure $|\boldsymbol{B}_{\rm tot}|^2 / 4\pi \ge \xi \rho (v_\perp^2 + c_s^2)$, yielding parallel velocity profile $v_\parallel^2(\ell) = v_{\parallel,\rm load}^2 + 2 G M_1 [r(\ell)^{-1} - r_{\rm load}^{-1}]$ and density profile $n_{\rm e}(\ell) = \Lambda B(\ell) / [\mu_{\rm e} m_{\rm p} v_\parallel(\ell)]$ to evaluate hollow-cone ECME radio visibility and energy-dependent X-ray transfer.
assumptions: The white dwarf magnetic field captures the accretion stream once magnetic pressure exceeds the stream hydrodynamic pressure: $|\boldsymbol{B}_{\rm tot}|^2 / 4\pi \ge \xi \rho (v_\perp^2 + c_s^2)$.

ECME operates when the electron plasma-to-cyclotron frequency ratio remains below the critical threshold $\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_B \le 0.3$ via a loss-cone distribution $\sin^2\alpha_{\rm lc}(\ell) = B(\ell)/B_{\rm m}$.
limits: Establishing the general evolutionary sequence connecting LPTs and mCVs requires larger, well-characterized observational samples and continuous multiwavelength monitoring.

We investigate this coexistence using a unified mass-loading framework for”
III Unified Mass-loading Framework: “The WD magnetic field captures the accretion flow if the magnetic pressure dominates the flow’s hydrodynamic pressure.”
III.2.1 Electron-Cyclotron Maser Emission: “A loss-cone distribution can be produced when electrons propagate into the converging field toward the WD.”

IV.2 Radio emission: “Within the coloured region, the electron density spans $n_{\rm e}\sim(1-4)\times 10^{7}~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, giving $\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_{\rm B}\sim 0.03-0.06$, comfortably below the adopted ECME limit of 0.3.”

V.4.2 Evolutionary ordering and the status of J1745: “Establishing the proposed evolutionary connection between LPTs and mCVs requires larger, well-characterized samples and continuous multiwavelength observations.”

The coloured contour, coded by electron density $\log_{10}(n_{\rm e}/{\rm cm^{-3}})$, demonstrates the region that satisfies all adopted cyclotron-frequency, maser-production, and beaming criteria at the reference phase. This coloured region is the envelope of accepted tubes: not every flux tube passing through its projected area is radio-capable. (b) Orbital variation of the emission–observer angular mismatch $\alpha(\phi)$ for a representative allowed sample. Visibility requires $\alpha(\phi)\leq\theta_{b}$. The shaded interval marks the resulting visibility window near the conjunction at $\phi=0.25$. (c) Number of radio-capable flux tubes visible to the observer as a function of orbital phase. Visible tubes occur only within the window around $\phi=0.25$. Tube counts are a geometric visibility diagnostic and should not be interpreted as radio flux.

figures.caption: Figure 9: Dependence of the X-ray phase geometry on WD dipole orientation and mass-transfer rate. analysis.reason: The paper provides an extensive 12-year NuSTAR timing and spectral analysis (3–79 keV across 27 epochs) of the TeV blazar Mrk 421, delivering concrete scaling relations for synchrotron peak shifts and flux distributions relevant to relativistic jet dynamics and particle acceleration.
analysis.result: Mrk 421 exhibits extreme hard X-ray flux variability spanning a factor of 200–225 over 12 years (with an intra-day $P_{\rm var}$ up to $73\%$). The flux PDF favors a lognormal distribution (reduced $\chi^2 \sim 7$ versus $\sim 35$ for normal), accompanied by a linear RMS–flux relation ($r_s = 0.77$, $p = 4.38 \times 10^{-6}$). analysis.result: In the MAD state, the total angular momentum flux is radially conserved ($\propto r^{-0.01}$), with $96\%$–$105\%$ carried outward by the coherent Blandford–Znajek jet channel ($\propto r^{-0.08}$) dominated by laminar Maxwell stress $-\langle b^r\rangle\langle b_\varphi\rangle$. The effective viscous stress parameter scales as $\alpha_{\rm visc} \propto r^{-0.30}$ in MAD, $r^{-0.56}$ in INT, and $r^{-0.35}$ in SANE, resulting in a viscous timescale $t_{\rm visc}/t_{\rm dyn} \approx 84$–$93$ at $10$–$40\,r_g$ in MAD (accelerating disk evolution by a factor of $\sim 3.5$–$4.5$ relative to SANE). During flux eruptions triggered by magnetic interchange instability, the horizon magnetic flux $\phi_{r_H}$ drops by up to $52.0\%$ (from $53.95$ to $25.87$) and mass accretion rate $|\dot{M}|_{r_H}$ drops by $40.6\%$, accompanied by a net sign reversal of angular momentum flux across the jet boundary at $10\,r_g$ (from $+2.19$ to $-0.90$), a doubling of jet tilt angle $\theta_{\rm tilt}$ from $9.21^\circ$ to $21.87^\circ$, and funnel narrowing ($\theta_{\rm open}$ contracting by $5\%$ to $62.85^\circ$).

analysis.reason: The paper provides a foundational kinetic breakthrough by uncovering that plasmoids in relativistic magnetic reconnection are born via Weibel-driven current filamentation induced by counter-streaming carrier anisotropy at the primary x-line, with the instability quenched at an isotropization scale $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim \frac{1+\sigma_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}} d_0$, governing plasmoid formation and reconnection morphology in relativistic jets and magnetar environments.
analysis.result: The authors find that plasmoids are initiated by a transverse electromagnetic current-filamentation/Weibel instability driven by extreme counter-streaming drift anisotropy ($z$-axis) near the primary x-line, rather than traditional Harris-sheet tearing. The dispersion relation in the cold limit yields a maximum growth rate $\Gamma_{\rm max} = \omega_p \beta_J \langle 1/\gamma \rangle^{1/2} \eta$ with $\beta_J^2 \equiv \langle \beta_z^2 / \gamma \rangle / \langle 1 / \gamma \rangle$ and measured growth $\Gamma_{\rm max} \sim 0.1\,\omega_{p0}$ peaking near upstream magnetization $\sigma_0 \sim 10$ (scaling as $\Gamma_{\rm max}/\omega_{p0} \propto \sigma_0^{1/2}$ in non-relativistic regimes). Plasma loading accumulates sheet surface density $\Sigma \sim n_0 \beta_{\rm rec} \ell (v_{A0}/v_{\rm out})$, reducing drift velocity $\beta_z \propto 1/\ell$ and effective anisotropy ratio $\frac{\Theta_z'}{\Theta_x'} \approx (1+\sigma_0)^2 \left( \frac{d_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}\ell} \right)^2$, completely quenching filamentation beyond the isotropization scale $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim \frac{1+\sigma_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}} d_0$ (or $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim 10\sigma_0 d_0$ for high $\sigma_0$ with reconnection rate $\beta_{\rm rec} \sim 0.1$).
analysis.reading_entry: III X-line Anisotropy Drives Current Filamentation
analysis.problem: The microphysical trigger and driver of secondary tearing and plasmoid birth in relativistic kinetic reconnection layers, as well as why and where secondary plasmoid generation is suppressed along the reconnection layer, have remained poorly understood.
analysis.method: Two-dimensional relativistic PIC simulations using Tristan-MP v2 across $0.1 \le \sigma_0 \le 1000$ in anti-parallel pair plasma sheets, coupled with linear Vlasov-Maxwell stability analysis deriving the dispersion relation $c^2 k^2 (1 + M^2) = \omega_p^2 [\theta_x^{-1} W(\zeta) \langle \beta_z^2 / \gamma \rangle - \langle (1 - \beta_z^2) / \gamma \rangle]$ (where $\zeta = M / \sqrt{2\theta_x}$) and marginal stability marginalization for thermal quenching.
citation_leads: The Birth of Plasmoids: Weibel-Driven Secondary Tearing and its Suppression in Relativistic Reconnection: “Plasmoids, or magnetic islands, dominate relativistic reconnection layers in kinetic simulations, yet the instability that creates them remains poorly understood.”
IV Plasma loading shuts off filamentation: “The sheet must therefore accumulate more plasma before it becomes isotropic, extending the unstable region.”
A.1 Derivation: “Define $\beta_{J}^{2}\equiv\langle\beta_{z}^{2}/\gamma\rangle/\langle 1/\gamma\rangle$, the inertia-weighted mean-square drift velocity, and $\gamma_{J}^{2}=1/(1-\beta_{J}^{2})$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that plasmoids originate from a Weibel-type kinetic current filamentation rather than sheared-field tearing mode, and derived the critical spatial cutoff scale $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim \frac{1+\sigma_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}} d_0$ set by plasma loading beyond which plasmoid generation ceases.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a 1D self-similar, special-relativistic, grey radiative transfer hydrodynamic model for expanding accretion layers, demonstrating that non-stationary evolution alters the emergent angular intensity contrast $C = I(0.1)/I(1)$ by up to tens of percent.
analysis.result: Time-dependent expansion and heating fundamentally alter the emergent angular contrast $C = I_s(0.1)/I_s(1)$. As dimensionless heating increases from $\mathcal{H}=0$ to $\mathcal{H}=4$, the emergent radiation transitions from limb darkening ($C = 0.436$) to limb brightening ($C = 1.264$). In comparison to stationary frozen-source benchmarks, the relative correction $(C_{\rm TD}/C_{\rm FS})-1 = (e_{0.1}-e_1)/(1+e_1)$ changes sign from $+31\%$ in optically thin, fast-expanding layers ($\tau_0 \sim 0.12$) to $-5.9\%$ in thicker layers ($\tau_0 \sim 0.9$), driven by oblique photon flight paths sampling non-negligible flow age fractions $(t-t_b)/t = (\eta_s-\eta_b)/(\mu-\eta_b)$.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.3 Why the contrast can change sign
analysis.problem: Whether time-dependent propagation effects in dynamic, expanding accretion flows (such as super-Eddington winds and tidal disruption events) break stationary radiative transfer assumptions and modify emergent angular intensity profiles when photon flight times are comparable to the expansion timescale.
analysis.method: A 1D plane-parallel, grey, special-relativistic self-similar radiation hydrodynamics formulation in similarity coordinate $\eta = z/(ct)$, with density $\rho_0 = R(\eta)/(\chi ct)$ and radiative intensity $I = \frac{c^2}{4\pi\chi t} i(\eta,\mu)$. The conservative transport equation $\frac{\partial}{\partial\eta}[(\mu-\eta)i] = R(D^3 s_0 - D^{-1}i)$ (where Doppler factor $D = [\gamma(1-\beta\mu)]^{-1}$) is coupled directly to mass continuity $C_m = \gamma R(\beta-\eta)$ and radiative acceleration $\gamma^3 (\beta-\eta)\beta' = h_0$ without ad-hoc Eddington closures, solved via an upwind finite-volume scheme and Gauss-Legendre angular quadrature.
assumptions: Planar, 1D self-similar relativistic expansion where geometric thickness scales as $\propto t$ and optical depth $\tau_0 = \int_{\eta_b}^{\eta_s} R\,d\eta$ remains constant in time.
Gas pressure, gravity, and magnetic stresses are neglected (cold matter approximation, where acceleration is purely radiative).
limits: Applies strictly above an unspecified launching region without self-consistent gravitational potential or thermal gas dynamics.
citation_leads: 2.3 Radiation and acceleration: “For the prescribed positive mass flux $C_{m}>0$, positive density requires $\beta>\eta$. This selects gas moving upward relative to surfaces of fixed $\eta$; it is not a restriction on all possible similarity flows.”
4.1 Heating and limb brightening: “The outward rise of density also follows from the evolving geometry. Continuity conserves $\gamma R(\beta-\eta)$, not the stationary-flow quantity $\gamma R\beta$.”
4.3 Why the contrast can change sign: “For positive normal intensity, the contrast correction is negative whenever the fractional enhancement along the normal exceeds that along the oblique ray.”
5.5 Domain of the model: “Gravity, gas pressure and magnetic stresses are absent, so the gas enters with a prescribed velocity and the solution applies above an unspecified launching region.”

analysis.reason: The paper develops a self-consistent magnetically heated slim disc-corona model across near- to super-Eddington regimes, providing physical scalings and spectral tables to interpret TDE X-ray spectral transitions.
analysis.result: The model successfully accounts for the spectral and temporal evolution of TDE AT2021ehb, deriving a black hole mass $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.317\pm 0.055$. The accretion rate follows a power-law decay $\dot{m}_{\rm XRT}=0.44(t/120\,{\rm d})^{-1.60}$, while rapid hardening is driven by a $\sim 300$-fold drop in the plasma parameter $\beta=(p_{\rm gas}+p_{\rm rad})/p_{\rm B}$. A lower limit for Comptonized photon index $\Gamma \sim 2$ is established due to disk reprocessing seed photons.
analysis.problem: Standard thin disc-corona and slim disc models suffer from unphysical discontinuities across radiation- and gas-pressure dominated regimes, and fail to self-consistently explain the rapid X-ray brightening, state transitions, and hard coronal emission observed in TDEs like AT2021ehb.
analysis.method: A unified set of slim disc equations is solved simultaneously incorporating gas pressure $p_{\rm gas}$, radiation pressure $p_{\rm rad}$, magnetic pressure $p_{\rm B}$, advection cooling $Q_{\rm adv}^- = \frac{\dot{M}}{4\pi R^2}\frac{p}{\rho_{\rm d}}\xi$, and coronal dissipation $Q_{\rm cor}^- = \frac{B^2}{4\pi}V_{\rm A}$, coupled to vertical hydrostatic equilibrium $p/\rho_{\rm d}=\Omega_{\rm K}^2 H^2$ and local energy conservation $(Q_{\rm vis}^+-Q_{\rm adv}^-)(1-f_{\rm c})=Q_{\rm rad}^-$. Hard X-ray Comptonization spectra are evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations.

analysis.reason: This work explores gravitational-wave memory signals produced by relativistic MHD jets from short GRBs, offering concrete waveforms and spectral signatures relevant to compact object central engines.
analysis.result: The sGRB relativistic jet generates a memory-type gravitational-wave signal with low-frequency strain amplitude $|\tilde{h}(f)| \propto 1/f$ and a characteristic knee at $f \sim 0.3\text{--}0.5\,\mathrm{Hz}$ set by the injection duration $t_{\rm inj} = 2\,\mathrm{s}$. At $D = 10\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, the strain plateau reaches $h_{+} \simeq 2.5 \times 10^{-24}$ for $\theta_v = 30^{\circ}\text{--}40^{\circ}$, accompanied by an early negative dip at $t' \approx 0.044\,\mathrm{s}$ caused by lateral equatorial momentum exchange from Poynting flux.
analysis.problem: Standard gravitational-wave quadrupole approximations fail for ultra-relativistic collimated outflows, making it necessary to develop numerical retarded integration to evaluate GW waveforms, memory features, and detectability from sGRB MHD jets.
analysis.method: Direct volume integration of retarded linearized Einstein equations in the wave zone without quadrupole approximations, splitting $T_{ij} = T_{ij}^{(\mathrm{matter})} + T_{ij}^{(\mathrm{EM})}$ into kinetic, electric, and magnetic contributions, post-processing 2D axisymmetric relativistic MHD simulations of a Poynting-dominated jet with luminosity $L = 4\times 10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg/s}$ expanding into merger ejecta.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Self-lensing signatures in the observed light curve for the static-hotspot case with $p=50\,M$ and $\theta_{o}=85^{\circ}$. Panel (a) shows the long-timescale light curve decomposed into odd- and even-event branches, together with their lensing envelopes. As the observer-relative azimuth $\phi_{o,\mathrm{rel}}$ drifts due to Lense-Thirring precession, each branch is periodically brought close to the optical axis and forms a broad magnification envelope. Adjacent envelope maxima in the combined odd-even sequence are separated by $T_{\mathrm{env}}=4.115\times 10^{5}\,M$. The inferred full nodal-precession period is therefore $T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{infer}}=2T_{\mathrm{env}}=8.231\times 10^{5}\,M$, consistent with $T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{th}}=8.278\times 10^{5}\,M$. Panel (b) zooms into the even-event envelope over $\phi_{o,\mathrm{rel}}=195^{\circ}$ to $165^{\circ}$. The recurrence time within each branch remains approximately constant, as observed in GSN 069 [ 30, 46, 50 ]. Panel (c) shows the local short-timescale light curve near the envelope shoulder. Self-lensing naturally imprints a strong-weak flare pattern on top of the intrinsic long-short recurrence pattern. Panel (d) decomposes the flares in Panel (c) into low-order image components. We retain the $N=0$ and $N=1$ images because higher-order images are strongly demagnified. Far-side events produce components with different magnifications, $\mu_{1}$ and $\mu_{2}$, and a finite delay $\Delta t$. The direct image, with $\mu_{\mathrm{dir}}\simeq 1$, traces the near-side emission pattern.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Lense–Thirring precession shifts the observer-relative azimuth of successive disk-crossing flares, producing broad magnification envelopes and alternating strong and weak flares. The envelope spacing gives an inferred full precession period of $T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{infer}}=2T_{\mathrm{env}}=8.231\times10^{5}\,M$, consistent with the theoretical value $T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{th}}=8.278\times10^{5}\,M$.

figures.caption: Figure 6: Lensing signatures of Keplerian hotspots following two adjacent disk-crossing events of the fiducial EMRI orbit, viewed at $\theta_{o}=88^{\circ}$. Panel (a) shows the equatorial-plane geometry. The light- and dark-red regions mark $\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}\geq 1.5$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}\geq 5$, respectively. Since the EMRI orbit is eccentric, Events 1 and 2 occur at different radii, $r_{s}=45.5\,M$ and $55.5\,M$, respectively. The Event 1 hotspot starts on the far side and moves through the strongly magnified region. By contrast, the Event 2 hotspot starts on the near side and remains direct-image dominated. Panel (b) shows the time-dependent magnifications of the $N=0$ and $N=1$ lensed images for Event 1. The inter-image delay also varies as the hotspot moves, being larger near the beginning and end of the curves and smaller in between. The two magnification peaks are separated by approximately $2.7\,M$ in observer time. Panel (c) compares the intrinsic flare, the two image contributions, and total observed light curve. The peak of the evolving magnification occurs after the intrinsic luminosity peak, enhancing the declining wing and producing a trailing shoulder.

analysis.reason: Investigates whether Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion observables (timing lags, QPOs, accretion rate) can constrain regular black holes with a de Sitter core, establishing an observational degeneracy limit with standard Schwarzschild black holes for high-energy compact object timing studies.
analysis.result: Due to the exponential screening factor $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2 M)}$, corrections to the metric decay rapidly outside the horizon. Even for near-extremal critical scales $l_{\rm cr} = 1.1M$ where gravitational acceleration deviates by $\delta g/g_{\rm S} \approx 12\%$ at $r = 2.3M$, the hydrodynamic impact is strictly confined to $r \lesssim 2.7M$. Across all models, time-averaged accretion rates differ from Schwarzschild by $|\Delta \langle \dot{M} \rangle| / \langle \dot{M} \rangle < 0.8\%$ ($2\sigma$), the shock-cone opening angle remains $1.077 \pm 0.003\ \mathrm{rad}$, the stagnation radius is $r_{\rm st} = 26.8 \pm 0.3M$, and inward fluctuation propagation lags ($\tau_{12 \to 6.11} = 75.5 \pm 1.0M$ and $\tau_{6.11 \to 2.3} = 31.6 \pm 0.4M$) agree within $1.6\%$, rendering the de Sitter core undetectable via accretion timing.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.1 Shock-cone morphology and the local response to the core
analysis.problem: Whether the de Sitter regular core replacing the central singularity in Dymnikova black holes can produce detectable signatures in relativistic Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion flow observables (such as mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, shock-cone geometry, QPOs, and time lags) in high-energy compact objects.
analysis.method: 2D equatorial general relativistic hydrodynamics (GRHD) simulations of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion onto fixed Dymnikova backgrounds ($0.1M \le l_{\rm cr} \le 1.1M$, up to $97\%$ of extremal limit $l_{\rm cr}^{\rm ext} = 1.1379M$) with lapse $f(r) = 1 - 2M(1 - e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2 M)})/r$, combined with Whittle-likelihood power spectrum analysis, ensemble averaging, and cross-spectral time lag diagnostics $\tau_{a\to b}(f) = \arg[G_{ab}(f)]/(2\pi f)$.
assumptions: The black hole is non-rotating, spherically symmetric, and adequately described by the Dymnikova metric with critical length scale $l_{\rm cr} < l_{\rm cr}^{\rm ext} = 1.1379M$.
limits: Simulations are restricted to 2D equatorial Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton flows without magnetic fields (GRMHD) or radiation transport.

analysis.result: Decomposition reveals an accretion disk continuum fraction of $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.37^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$ (mean jet polarization $\bar{p}_{\mathrm{j}} = 3.60^{+0.03}_{-0.03}\%$, $\tau_{\mathrm{H}\beta} = 54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}\,\mathrm{days}$) for PKS 1510-089, and $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$ ($\bar{p}_{\mathrm{j}} = 2.05^{+0.03}_{-0.02}\%$, $\tau_{\mathrm{H}\beta} = 84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}\,\mathrm{days}$) for PKS 0736+017, moving corrected disk luminosities closer to the canonical $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}-L_{5100}$ relation.

analysis.problem: In flat-spectrum radio quasars, intense Doppler-boosted non-thermal synchrotron emission from relativistic jets heavily contaminates optical continuum emission, decoupling continuum from broad emission line variability and distorting the canonical $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}-L_{5100}$ relationship and black hole mass estimates.
analysis.method: Bayesian light-curve decomposition framework (DECOMP) modeling disk $C_d(t)$ and jet $C_j(t)$ as independent Damped Random Walk (DRW) processes with covariance $S_{\star}(\Delta t) = \sigma_{\star}^{2}\exp(-|\Delta t|/T_{\star})$, convolving with Gaussian transfer functions $\Psi(\tau) = \frac{f_{\star}}{\sqrt{2\pi\omega_{\star}^2}}\exp\left[-\frac{(\tau-\tau_{\star})^2}{2\omega_{\star}^2}\right]$ for $\mathrm{H}\beta$ and 37 GHz radio curves, coupled with Stokes parameters ($I, Q, U$) and polarization constraints.
assumptions: The accretion disk optical emission has negligible intrinsic polarization ($p_{\mathrm{d}}=0$) relative to the synchrotron jet emission.
limits: Using 37 GHz light curves as the jet driving template lags behind compact optical synchrotron emission zones due to synchrotron self-absorption, limiting fidelity during rapid, violent blazar flaring.

analysis.research_progress: Establishes the largest jet position angle swing ($57^{\circ}\pm 8^{\circ}$) detected to date in GRS 1915+105, directly ruling out slim-disc Lense-Thirring precession due to severe timescale discrepancy ($P_{\rm prec}\sim 27\,\mathrm{s}$ vs observed months) and establishing radiation-driven disc warping as the driver of both jet precession and line-of-sight obscuration.

focus_paper.title: Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays

must_read.label: Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays
must_read.text: Fitting Pierre Auger Phase I data reveals that UHECR observations strongly favor a two-component BNSM model at $\ge 7.2\sigma$ over single-component models.

must_read.label: A temporally clustered gravitational wave pair and a Type IIb supernova
must_read.text: The GW pair S190910d and S190910h separated by $\Delta t \simeq 7.1\,\mathrm{hr}$ has a pairwise null chance coincidence probability of $P_{\rm 2GW} = 7.6 \times 10^{-5}$ under 3D localization overlap tests.

must_read.label: The Birth of Plasmoids: Weibel-Driven Secondary Tearing and its Suppression in Relativistic Reconnection
must_read.text: The authors find that plasmoids are initiated by a transverse electromagnetic current-filamentation/Weibel instability driven by extreme counter-streaming drift anisotropy ($z$-axis) near the primary x-line, rather than traditional Harris-sheet tearing.

key_highlights.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
key_highlights.result: The combined all-flavor neutrino flux of the 28 candidates reaches $E_{\nu}^{2}\Phi_{\nu} \sim (1-3) \times 10^{-9}\ {\rm GeV\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}\ sr^{-1}}$, contributing $1-3\%$ of the diffuse flux measured at $\sim 10\ {\rm TeV}$.

key_highlights.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
key_highlights.result: For low-polarization superluminal quasars (LPSQs; $P_{\rm opt} < 3\%$ and apparent speeds $\beta_{\rm app}c = 5c - 31c$), the duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $\psi > 5\%$) is suppressed to $0\%$ under standard $F_\eta$ tests and only $\approx 7\%$ under the enhanced $F$-test, which is 3-10 times lower than in high-polarization quasars (HPQs, $\mathrm{DC} \sim 30\%$), demonstrating that high optical linear polarization rather than relativistic Doppler boosting is the primary driver and diagnostic of INOV.

key_highlights.title: Probing the geometry and outflows of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 with multi-band polarimetry
key_highlights.result: Optical linear polarisation is detected at $P = 0.3\text{--}1.5\%$ across $R$ and $I$ bands.
